summary: Wolfram Eberhard studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1927–1933) and worked in sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Ankara University (~1937–1948) and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun works in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Stony Brook University. He held a post as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University, attested in 2012.

Woosung Huh works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hawaii. Attested in 2012, he served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.

Wu Hung studied at Harvard University (~1980–1987) and works in history, archaeology, and sinology. Around 1994, he held posts at the Smart Museum of Art and as a professor at the University of Chicago.
Wulstan Fletcher works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 1999, he studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche.
Xianda studied Buddhist studies, earning a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2016). His teachers included K. L. Dhammajoti and Toshiichi Endo.

Xianlin Ji studied at Tsinghua University (1930–1934) and the University of Göttingen (1935–1941), working in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Göttingen (1937) and Peking University, where he became Life Professor in 1980.

Xiaoling Wu worked in sinology and Indology. He held positions at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), Peking University, Academia Sinica (~1950–1977), and served as a professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoting Wei works in sinology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2004, Wei earned an MA from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng-Mei Ku.

Xinchuan Huang studied at Peking University (~1954–1958) and worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from around 1977 to 2021, including as a researcher (~1977–2000).

Xinru Liu studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), working in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2010) and The College of New Jersey (~2000–2021).
Xiuzhi Zeng works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2006, Zeng completed an MA at Nanhua University under the supervision of Meihua Chen.

Xuesong Zhang studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Xueyu (PhD attested 2008). Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Zhang was an associate professor at Renmin University of China, attested in 2015.

Xuezhu Li studied under Shoryu Katsura in the fields of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post as a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011) and as Research Associate at China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2017).

Y. Karunadasa completed doctoral studies under David Friedman at the University of London (~1960–1963) in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as Director at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1989–2000, attested 2008) and professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2013).

Yael Bentor studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University, completing doctoral work under Gregory Schopen in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, she taught in the Department of Indian Studies at the Hebrew University.
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies and sinology, completing a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An studied Buddhist studies, earning a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich by 1998, and also studied under Hojin (attested 2003).
Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetology scholar who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. Attested in 2012, Chen earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
